questions.question: Which protocol is used for video conferencing and live streaming applications such as Zoom and Skype?
questions.explanation: RTP (Real-Time Transport Protocol) carries live audio/video for conferencing; RTSP controls media sessions like play and pause.

questions.question: What is the codename of Android 14?
questions.explanation: Android 13 is Tiramisu, Android 14 is Upside Down Cake (2023), Android 15 is Vanilla Ice Cream and Android 16 is Baklava.

questions.question: What is the output of print(2 * 3 ** 3)?
questions.explanation: ** has higher precedence than *, so 3 ** 3 = 27 is computed first, then 2 * 27 = 54. Evaluating left to right gives 6 ** 3 = 216.

questions.concept: Primitive data types keep Java from being 100% object oriented
questions.question: Smalltalk is considered 100% object oriented, but Java is not. What is the main reason?

options.A: Java requires a main() method in every class
options.B: Java allows primitive data types such as int, float and char
options.C: Java programs are compiled into bytecode first
options.D: Java supports static members only through interfaces

questions.explanation: In a pure object-oriented language every value is an object. Java keeps primitive types like int, float and char that are not objects, so it is not 100% object oriented.

questions.question: In 4G LTE IoT, what does LTE stand for?
questions.explanation: LTE stands for Long-Term Evolution, the successor of 3G and 2G smartphone technology.

questions.concept: Life cycle model describes entry and exit criteria of phases
questions.question: A project manager needs a description of when each phase may begin and what must be complete before it ends. Which of these provides the entry and exit criteria for each phase?
questions.explanation: A system (software) life cycle model describes the entry and exit criteria for each phase. A CASE repository stores project information, a patch is an emergency fix and test cases verify behaviour.

questions.question: SMTP is mainly concerned with which part of an e-mail?

options.B: The message header and recipient addresses
options.D: The content of the message body

questions.explanation: SMTP uses the header and destination addresses; it is not concerned with the body content.

questions.question: Which of the following is given as an example of a 'thing' in IoT?

options.C: A farm animal with a biochip transponder

questions.explanation: A thing can be a person with a monitor implant, a farm animal with a biochip transponder or a car with built-in sensors; it must be able to sense and communicate.

questions.concept: Insertion sort state after inserting the fourth element
questions.question: Insertion sort (ascending) is applied to [8, 7, 13, 1, -9, 4]. What is the list immediately after the element 1 has been inserted into the sorted part?
questions.explanation: After inserting 7 and 13 the sorted part is [7, 8, 13]; 1 is smaller than all of them, so they shift right and 1 goes to the front: [1, 7, 8, 13, -9, 4].

questions.question: Automata, as abstract machines and mathematical models, are used in which pair of areas?

options.A: Compiler design and natural language processing

questions.explanation: Automata are used in compiler design and natural language processing.

questions.question: Phishing is an online crime carried out mainly through:

options.B: emails and fake websites or links

questions.explanation: Phishing uses emails, links and websites; SMS based attacks are smishing and VoIP voice calls are vishing.

questions.concept: Function header syntax with def and colon
questions.question: Which line is a correct header for a user-defined function in Python?
questions.explanation: A function definition begins with def, and the header ends with a colon.

questions.concept: Height of a tree measured in edges
questions.question: A tree has root A with children B and C; B has child D; D has child E; C has no children. What is the height of the tree (longest path from root to a leaf, counted in edges)?
questions.explanation: The longest root-to-leaf path is A-B-D-E, which has 3 edges. Counting nodes instead of edges gives 4.

questions.question: WPA2 is used to provide security for:
questions.explanation: WPA2 is used for Wi-Fi security; PGP secures email, TLS protects HTTP and AES is used in most ATMs.

questions.question: Which branch of Theory of Computation is concerned with what can be computed and what cannot be computed?
questions.explanation: Computability theory asks what can and cannot be computed; complexity theory asks why some problems are hard or easy.

questions.concept: Number of pages for 24-bit logical address and 1K page
questions.question: A system has a 24-bit logical address, a 16-bit physical address and a page size of 1 KB. How many pages are in the logical address space?
questions.explanation: Offset = 10 bits, so page bits = 24 - 10 = 14 and pages = 2^14 = 16384. 64 is the number of frames (2^6).

questions.question: Using a 3-variable K-map, what is the simplified form of F(A, B, C) = Σm(2, 3, 6, 7)?
questions.explanation: Minterms 010, 011, 110, 111 all have B = 1 while A and C vary, so the quad simplifies to F = B.

questions.concept: Foreign key needs matching data type and size
questions.question: GUARDIAN.GUID is declared CHAR(12). To run ALTER TABLE STUDENT ADD FOREIGN KEY(GUID) REFERENCES GUARDIAN(GUID); successfully, how must STUDENT.GUID be declared?

options.A: CHAR(12), matching the referenced type and size
options.B: INT, since GUID holds only digits
options.C: CHAR(10), since a smaller size is allowed
options.D: VARCHAR(20), since any string type is accepted

questions.explanation: A foreign key must have the same data type and size as the primary key it references, so STUDENT.GUID must also be CHAR(12).

questions.question: What is the output of print('world' in 'Hello World!')?
questions.explanation: The in operator checks for an exact substring and is case-sensitive. 'world' (lowercase w) does not occur in 'Hello World!'.

questions.question: Which graph representation stores, for each vertex, a list of its adjacent vertices?
questions.explanation: An adjacency list is a collection of lists where each vertex stores its adjacent vertices; an adjacency matrix is a 2-D matrix of vertices.

questions.question: What does the expression (A + B)·(A + B') simplify to?
questions.explanation: By distributive law (A + B)(A + B') = A + B·B' = A + 0 = A (complement and identity laws).

questions.question: An entity PERSON has an attribute Gender that holds exactly one value for each person. What type of attribute is Gender?
questions.explanation: A single-valued attribute has exactly one value, such as DOB or gender.

questions.concept: Dynamic binding used in implementing inheritance
questions.question: Which feature of OOP is used extensively in implementing inheritance?
questions.explanation: Inheritance relies heavily on dynamic binding, where the function to be called is resolved at run time based on the actual object.

questions.question: What is the native file extension of an Adobe Photoshop document?
questions.explanation: Photoshop saves documents as .psd (Photoshop Document); .ai belongs to Adobe Illustrator.

questions.question: What happens in an Ethernet hub when two connected devices send data at exactly the same time?

options.A: The hub queues one frame and forwards it later
options.C: The hub repacks the data into smaller packets
options.D: The data is delivered only to the intended device

questions.explanation: A hub sends data arriving on one line out on all others, so simultaneous transmissions collide.
